provenance: Lane split authored by the Stage-2 decision-agent (read-only; returns JSON in reply) and persisted by the orchestrator as the agent's returned detect-vs-hunt partition. Detection = seed complement of the agent's hunt set; validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup, and det-count reconciled against the agent's summary. All ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset. Per-technique rationale shows the Stage-1 detection-feasibility basis.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — mass port scanning (esp. RTSP/554 sweeps) against internet-facing assets is observable via perimeter/IDS, netflow and honeypot telemetry, though source IPs are VPN-fronted and attribution is hard
medium — web-app vulnerability scanning generates distinctive request patterns detectable via WAF/IDS and web-server log analysis
medium — the tools are legitimate, but their on-target use (SQLMap injection strings, Acunetix/Burp scan signatures) is detectable via WAF/IDS and web-log analytics

medium — SQL-injection and web-exploitation attempts are detectable via WAF/IPS signatures, anomalous web-server child-process spawns, and web-application logging; this is a primary DETECTION surface for the actor
medium — anomalous logins to streaming/display/admin panels from VPN ASNs and impossible-travel analytics can surface valid-account abuse, though it can resemble legitimate use
medium — msiexec spawning an unexpected child executable (bd.exe) and MSI package integrity/signing anomalies are detectable via process-creation and EDR telemetry
medium — repeated authentication failures across accounts/services are detectable via authentication-log analytics and lockout monitoring
medium — HTTP beaconing to the known WezRat C2 paths/domains and periodic web callbacks are detectable via network/proxy logging, DNS monitoring and IOC matching
medium — post-install downloads of executable content and new-binary drops correlated with process lineage are detectable via EDR and proxy telemetry
medium — RAT beaconing, command-line-launched implant behavior and the known WezRat hashes/C2 give a workable detection surface via EDR and network IOCs
medium — host-enumeration API/command patterns from a freshly-spawned implant are detectable via EDR behavioral analytics, though individually low-signal

medium — external defacement/content-injection is detectable via file-integrity monitoring, 'known-good' content baselining and external brand/surface monitoring; a DETECTION surface for the influence payoff

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — third-party database queries occur entirely off-victim and leave no defender-side telemetry; a HUNT/attack-surface-awareness item (know what of yours is indexed in Shodan) rather than a log detection
low — off-victim OSINT against public/commercial data sources; not observable in defender telemetry

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Gather Victim Identity Information: Email Addresses
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — email-address enumeration is off-victim; a threat-intel/hunt awareness item

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Gather Victim Identity Information: Employee Names
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — social-media reconnaissance is off-victim; not detectable in enterprise telemetry

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — off-victim geolocation reconnaissance; not detectable in defender telemetry

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Gather Victim Network Information: Domain Properties
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — passive subdomain enumeration via third-party services is off-victim; hunt via attack-surface monitoring of your own exposed subdomains
low — acquisition of leaked data is off-victim; the downstream credential reuse is where detection becomes feasible (authentication anomaly monitoring)
low — infrastructure acquisition is off-victim; a HUNT/attribution surface via reseller pivots and VPN-node reputation, and the advisory notes VPN nodes are shared so are not exclusive indicators
low — domain registration is off-victim; a HUNT signal via newly-registered/lookalike-domain feeds and persona-domain clustering
low — off-victim service acquisition; a hunt/attribution artifact rather than a host or log detection
low — persona creation is entirely off-victim; a HUNT/attribution artifact (persona-network mapping, avatar/handle reuse, cross-platform linkage), not a host or log detection
low — account creation is off-victim; only the inbound intimidation messages themselves are observable, on the recipient side
low — exploit development is off-victim; downstream exploitation attempts are the detection surface
low — staging on attacker infrastructure is off-victim; the resulting client callbacks (T1071.001) are the detection surface
low — offline hash cracking occurs entirely on attacker/third-party resources with no victim-side telemetry; a hunt/awareness item
low — obfuscation defeats static signatures; hunt via entropy analysis, the published WezRat detection content, and behavioral (decode-then-beacon) analytics

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — name/location masquerade defeats name-based trust; a HUNT via signer/metadata mismatch, MSI-behavior anomaly and lookalike-domain analysis

low — exfiltration to web services can blend with normal outbound web traffic; hunt via large/anomalous outbound transfers to newly-seen destinations and DLP, though the leak itself often surfaces externally first
